title: Questions 191-195 refer to the following e-mails and article.
passage_1:
To:Priya Raval <p.raval@ravaldental.com>
From:Tobias Lund <t.lund@northgatebuild.com>
Date:February 8
Subject:Fit-Out Plan

Dear Dr. Raval,

Following our first consultation about your dental clinic, Hana Okafor, our building surveyor, has finished her report on the empty printing works on Vale Street. The wide open floors are ideal for your treatment rooms, but the closeness of the tram depot makes it hard to keep those rooms quiet.

We propose a site visit on February 13, during which we will present our ideas for the building. My colleague, Ruben Diaz, who specialises in soundproofing, wants to show you a layered floor system. This will block almost all outside noise, which was your main worry. In addition, Grace Merton, our lead interior designer, will go over the layout of the waiting area and the staff room to make sure they suit your needs.

Please confirm whether this date suits you. We look forward to helping you build this quiet space.

Sincerely,
Tobias Lund
Project Manager, Northgate Build

To:Adele Sorensen <a.sorensen@sorensenvet.com>
From:Priya Raval <p.raval@ravaldental.com>
Date:February 11
Subject:A firm for your refit

Hi Adele,

I hear you are looking for a contractor to refit the Sorensen Veterinary Clinic. I strongly recommend Northgate Build, the firm currently working on my practice.

They are extremely professional and careful with detail. They also have a special referral policy. If you mention that I recommended them, they will give you a 12 percent reduction.

If you like, I can pass on the phone number of their project manager, Tobias Lund, so that you can speak with him directly.

Best,
Priya

City Health: New Life for Old Buildings

By Iris Calloway, County Review

July 2—The city’s old factory district is going through a striking change. The newest example is Raval Dental’s clinic, which officially opened last week inside a former printing works.

The clinic’s most impressive feature is how quiet it is. Although the building sits beside a busy transport yard, the treatment rooms are completely silent. This piece of engineering lets dentists talk with patients without any outside noise. “It is like walking into a sealed box,” said one local practitioner.

The success of this project has already brought the designers more work. Northgate Build confirmed that it has been hired to refit the Sorensen Veterinary Clinic two streets away, a sign of a new chapter for the district.
